item.title: Therapy Dogs Visiting Marshall This Year
item.description:
Therapy dogs will be visiting Marshall this year to provide comfort, reduce stress, and create a calming presence for students throughout the school day. These visits can help support students' emotional well-being and make school a more positive experience. Parents who prefer their child not interact with the therapy dogs should contact Ms. Chrissy at rolfesc@talawanda.org to honor their wishes.

item.description:
Marshall PTG is hosting a Coffee & Donuts meetup on Friday, October 30, 2026 before the Marshall Halloween Parade. Families can gather at the shelter house near the overflow parking lot from 8:50-9:30 a.m. to enjoy refreshments and meet other Marshall families. item.title: Health Education Curriculum Update - Erin's Law
item.description:
Ohio Senate Bill 288 (Erin's Law) requires updated health education curriculum including developmentally appropriate prevention education on sexual abuse and sexual violence for K-12 students. Instruction will occur October 12-26, 2026 across all grade levels. Families can review curriculum materials online (links provided for K-3, 4-6, 7-8, and 9-12 covering topics like social inclusion, dating violence, and suicide prevention), and parents may opt their students out. Contact your student's school counselor with questions.

item.title: Title I Reading Corner Program Information
item.description:
The Title I Reading Corner Classroom provides daily 30-minute small-group reading instruction for K-3 students at Marshall Elementary. Teachers Lisa Dyer and Shawna Dalton work with students on letter naming, phonemic awareness, phonics, vocabulary, fluency, comprehension, and writing. Students are selected based on assessments given at the beginning of the school year and in December, and are released from the program when they consistently meet grade-level benchmarks. Parents are welcome to contact teachers with questions about their child's reading progress.

Talawanda School District now uses Peachjar, a digital flyer delivery service, to share information about educational, athletic, cultural, and community opportunities with families. item.title: Volunteer and Visitor Policy Requirements
item.description:
All adult volunteers must have a volunteer application on file with the office each school year. After a second visit, parents must complete fingerprinting and a background check through the Central Registration Office at least 3 weeks prior to their event. Background checks are valid for 5 years. Contact Ruth Michael at 513-273-3101 for Central Registration.

item.title: Marshall Elementary September 2026 Menus
item.description:
Marshall Elementary's breakfast and lunch menus for September 2026 are now available. The breakfast menu includes items like Mini Maple Pancakes, French Toast Bites, Bagel Sandwiches, and Breakfast Pizza, with 100% fruit juice, fresh fruit, and choice of milk included with every breakfast. The lunch menu features Chili Cheese Dogs, Walking Tacos, Chicken Tenders, Detroit Deep Dish Pizza, and various other entrees, with choice of milk included with every lunch. School is closed for Labor Day (September 7-8) and September 18. All menus are subject to change based on product availability.

item.title: School Nurse Health Reminders for Students
item.description:
Nurse Tonja welcomes students back and provides important health reminders for the school year: - Medications: Required forms must be completed and medications brought by parent/guardian (not in backpacks) - Contact Information: Update the school with current phone numbers and emergency contacts - Extra Clothes: Keep spare clothes at school for accidents - Illness Policy: Keep children home if they have fever, vomiting, diarrhea, or are too sick to learn - Immunizations: Ensure all required immunizations are up-to-date - Medical Conditions: Notify the nurse of any new diagnoses, allergies, or health concerns

item.description:

Major breaks include Fall Break (Oct 16), Thanksgiving Break (Nov 23-27), Winter Break (Dec 21-31 + Jan 1), Spring Break (March 22-26). Special days include picture days, data collaboration days, professional development days, and parent-teacher conferences in October. The last day of school is May 27th.
